_doc: MVP starting rules. See design/DESIGN_RULES.md for why each value is what it is.

start._doc: A player's new island (Simulation.new_island): money, level, the 2x2 island, its Momo (Step 53: none -- the player works alone and chooses to hire the first), and `buildings` placed finished, each waiting at `stage` -- a ripe farm, so the first tap is a harvest and its money (Step 50). Tests start from the bare world (new_game).

clock._doc: A day is day_seconds of real time and starts in the morning (Day N, 00 s is daylight, as in the reference screens). Phases are fractions of the day; the sky, light and anything that cares about night read them from here.

progression._doc: Player level and per-building mastery. EXP is given for completed, meaningful actions (a harvest, a building finished, land bought, and a point for each finished sowing and watering so the first minutes answer every step) -- never for taps. exp_to_next[N-1] is the EXP from level N to N+1; past the list the last step grows by `growth`.

land._doc: Price of the k-th purchased cell (k = 0 for the first): round_to * ceil(base * growth^k / round_to). Only cells sharing an edge with owned land can be bought. invite_level (Step 50): from this player level -- or with at most one tile left free -- the next tile glows with its price when it is affordable, and the sea tip says so.

economy._doc: How many days of money history to keep (status/analytics read it).

unlocks._doc: What the player must reach before something can be used. Buildings carry their own `unlock` in buildings.json; research (Step 22) adds its own.

momo._doc: Momo agents. Names are translation keys momo.name.N, handed out in order. Hiring price of the k-th paid hire after the first Momo (k = 0 first) = round_to * ceil(base * growth^k / round_to); the first Momo costs hire.first (Step 53). Unassigned Momo wander their island at walk_speed tiles/s, resting rest_seconds between strolls, and sleep at night. An assigned Momo does its building's work by itself, each stage taking work_time_multiplier times the player's time (Step 50: 1.0 -- a Momo works as fast as a person, so automation never costs speed) (cooldowns are world rules and stay as they are); with works_at_night true they keep at it under the moon, as in the reference night scene. starve_seconds (Step 50): a watched building ready this long while nearer ones kept its Momo busy is visited first.

hire._doc: Step 53: the island's first Momo costs `first` (it used to come free) -- two or three harvests by hand, so the player earns first and then chooses; at 15 the pacing targets hold (design/INCREMENTAL_PACING.md, Step 53: 30 pushed a Momo's first earnings to 233 s against 90). Every later hire costs what it did before -- base * growth^k, k = 0 for the second Momo. Hires the legacy pays for (prestige rewards.momo_every) cost nothing and come first.

proficiency._doc: A Momo's skill at one kind of building grows with the stages it has finished there: reaching thresholds[i] stages gives level i+1, and its work there takes multipliers[level] of its usual Momo time (level 0 = 1.0). Skill is per building type and stays with the Momo.

watch._doc: Watched tiles: each Momo works the buildings on the tiles it watches, the nearest ready one first. A Momo assigned to a building (dragged, or by the manager) watches that building's tiles; the pencil edits the set. `base_tiles` is how many one Momo may watch before research (watch_tiles effects add). `auto` (Step 50): a building finished on tiles nobody watches is taken by the nearest Momo already at work with room. Step 53: only a Momo the player has placed (opted in); a newly hired Momo is never put to work by itself.

schedule._doc: Step 61: a Momo on the player's own order (Schedule) works its stops strictly in turn, one stage each. At a stop that cannot start for a reason that does not end by itself (inputs, a full store, power, every place taken) it waits wait_seconds, then goes on to the next stop -- the stop keeps its place and is tried again when its turn comes round. Cooldowns, a stage under way and construction are always waited out.

pace._doc: Step 58: the owner found the work and the Momo far too quick. work_scale multiplies the work time of every stage (the player's tap, a Momo's turn, a lab's study, a smelt -- buildings.json `seconds` and recipe seconds) and its floor, once, in BuildingSystem.stage_seconds; the waits after a stage (`cooldown`: crops drinking, ore settling) are world rules and stay. travel_scale divides a Momo's walking speed, once, in MomoSystem.walk_speed. Research, skills, the Clock Tower, legacy and offline time all multiply on top of these, as before. The game clock, the camera, UI and feedback animations and the day are not touched. Each action pays more to match (Step 58, the owner's 'keep the direct rewards'): every item's price and every stage's EXP and mastery doubled (x2 against the work's x2.5 -- money a minute stays a little lower than before, the frozen pacing targets hold; design/INCREMENTAL_BALANCE_REPORT.md 'Step 58'). Step 69: the owner found it still too quick -- work_scale 2.5 -> 6.25 (x2.5 again, of the data seconds: one multiplier, applied once per stage, never 2.5 x 2.5 x 2.5), and construction, a timer of its own, x2.5 by build_scale (BuildingSystem.build_seconds_of). Walking, the waits, the day, research topic times and every price and EXP stay as they are: the owner wants a slower feel, not the old income back (design/INCREMENTAL_BALANCE_REPORT.md 'Step 69').

mail._doc: Momo Letters (data/letters.json). At most letters_per_day new letters arrive on one in-game day. Step 57: a letter that brings research (it is discovered on arrival) comes at least research_gap_seconds of game time after the previous one -- discoveries are paced by work, by days and by this gap, never by a delay in the UI.

offline._doc: Progress while the game is closed: the simulation runs the time away exactly as if open and untouched (assigned Momo, drip lines, waits, research, and the money finished work earns). Time away counts up to max_hours; at most max_events events are handled (the clock stops at the last one) -- a deterministic cost ceiling, never an estimate. A summary shows when at least report_seconds passed and something happened -- or, quietly, after quiet_report_seconds even if nothing did. autosave_seconds: how often the game saves while open (also when the window loses focus).

power._doc: Power is capacity, not stored energy: supply now (kW) against the draw of the buildings working now. A stage takes its power share when it starts -- satisfaction = supply / (draw of everything running + its own), capped at 1 -- and keeps that speed to its end (no continuous physics). Solar follows the sun (zero at night, peak at midday, the sky's own phases); wind follows a smooth deterministic gust curve (wind_* below) day and night; steam is steady while stoked; hydro is steady but needs the shore.

manager._doc: A Momo at an office manages: every review_seconds it moves at most moves_per_review workers -- never one the player placed (pinned) -- from a building idle and blocked for stuck_seconds, or set to off, to the highest-priority building with a free spot and work it can do; and it sends free Momo only to high-priority spots. Moves are walks, never instant.

community._doc: Momo life. Each Momo gets a home in id order from the homes' capacity (oldest homes first); unhoused Momo rest outdoors (rest 1.0). Island happiness 0..max_happiness is the sum of open amenities, each type counting its i-th copy at stack[i] (none beyond the list). Work time at a building is multiplied by the Momo's rest times (1 - happiness / max_happiness * happiness_effect), never below floor.

analytics._doc: The island's daily book (AnalyticsSystem): written from events, plus a look at power and idle buildings every sample_seconds; keep_days closed days are kept.

construction._doc: Demolishing a finished building returns this share of everything paid for it (building and refits), rounded down per item; cancelling one still under construction returns its type's `refund` (all of it).

prestige._doc: Selling the settlement (PrestigeSystem). Appraisal: every building's paid money x value.buildings (by family), land bought x value.land, daily sale+release income (last 7 days) x value.income_days, each Momo value.momo_base + value.momo_per_skill per skill level, completed research money cost x value.research, all experience gained x value.exp. Net value = appraisal - the head start the island was given. Legacy points ever earned = floor(sqrt(lifetime net / points_unit)); a sale adds what it lifts that by. Selling needs player level min_level. Points give, permanently: rewards.money_per_point starting money each, a free hire every rewards.momo_every (at most max_momos; Step 53: hires the player makes on the new island, which starts with no Momo), and Momo work time x (1 - work_per_point per point, at most work_cap).

research._doc: Research levels. A node can be researched again up to its max_level (5 unless its effects are switches -- auto, recipe, variety, power_use -- which stop at 1, or the node sets max_level). Level L costs money x level_cost_growth^(L-1) and items x level_item_growth^(L-1) -- never more of an item than the store can hold, so every level can be reached -- and takes seconds x level_time_growth^(L-1); its effects grow by level_strength per level past the first: a multiply m becomes m^(1 + level_strength x (L-1)), an add becomes add x (1 + level_strength x (L-1)). At Prestige every level researched in that run becomes one research point (RP) for good; RP are allocated to unlocked nodes as levels, freely re-allocated, never minted twice. reveal_ahead (Step 71): the research screen shows a topic once it is open, ever opened or researched, or opens within this many player levels with its prerequisites known -- the tree grows with the level instead of showing everything at once.

specials._doc: Special structures: how many may stand at once (`slots`, one village special until settlement tiers raise it).

journey._doc: The island's journey (Records): the levels whose first arrival is kept, with played, offline and wall time.

tiers._doc: Settlement tiers (TierSystem): village -> city -> nation. `special_slots` is how many special structures may stand at once at that tier (in total). `needs` are the milestones to promote INTO that tier: tiles owned, Momo living on the island, research levels active (sum), and produced value (lifetime money from sales and releases).
